Hi Coaches, our next presenter is the Chief of Tennis at Tennis Australia in Tom Larner. Tom heads up the participation side of the organisation and was a key driver in the latest coach review and he is here today to share some of those findings with you. Tom, thanks for your time and welcome. Well welcome everyone and thanks for taking the time to be part of the coach review stage of this piece. So I'm going to take you through the review process, what we've been through, some of the findings we've had and obviously you know what changes we're looking to make as part of the review which has happened over the last six months. Very much our objective was looking at how we can make coaches throughout Australia successful both on the court and off the court. Looking at what we're doing well, what we can do better and where we really should prioritise our time to support coaches in being successful. So over the past six months as I said really we've spent a lot of time doing a lot of research probably certainly in my time in tennis over the last 15 or so years more than we've looked at how coaches are performing before we've spoken to more coaches than we ever have and diagnosing what are the challenges that are facing the coaching community and what are those things we need to overcome to make coaching you know a better, more professional and more successful industry. We've been working through since then you know what are the things we can do based off

So in terms of the consultation phase as I said it was great that we had such a great response from our coach members over 600 respondees that it came back and provided quite a bit of detail in relation to the challenges they face, what we're doing well, where we can assist better in helping them be as I said more successful. We ran in person workshops right across Australia of virtual as well with coaches with our member association CEOs and a coach development team. We were from right across Australia we interviewed 36 private coaches directly and sought their feedback. People who have had a long history in the industry and working in that environment looked and worked with two other coaching organisations, identified three different domestic sports, what they were doing, what they had done well, what their coaching network had felt was most beneficial for them, we spoke and dealt with seven other international tennis federations or national tennis federations across the globe in relation to their and looked at their coaching membership, their coach education development and how they supported their coaches. We also formed a steering committee which had member association representation as well as representation from the coaching industry in helping us look at this look at the data that came back and look at how we could work with the coaching network to support them better. And you can see there on the slide as well the respondees and this is one of the challenges we want to overcome and one of the improvements we want to make in our sport is that 78% of those were male and 22% were female and we certainly recognise that need to grow the number of female coaches across the network as well. So from those discussions, there are really nine key themes or findings that had come through the coach review. Firstly, as a positive, generally the coach membership and the coaching industry felt that the courses were delivered well, they were delivered by professionals and the content was very good. So both in terms of obviously the content education development but also the external deliverers that were appointed to assist our team in delivering coach education. Probably for me one of the most concerning aspects of the feedback was the number two that coaches are unlikely to promote coaching as a job and we had two key areas that were really shone through as those, the key reasons why that was the case. The first was the lack of job security and I think probably that was highlighted in the

So there's a number of other pieces of information that were fed through there and fed into sort of things where we'll be looking to address and how we can improve the environment for coaches. So we've heard loud and clear through this review that we've done reviews before and there hasn't always been changes come out of those reviews. So certainly for me coming to the role of Chief Tennis Officer after being on the event side of the business for a long period of time, I'm very keen to make sure that what we've heard and from the industry that we do act on and we're starting to implement some of those changes already in relation to changing our membership program that you've already noticed. And finally, number nine, many coaches do not complete ongoing continuous professional development, CPD, and how we integrate that into our professional education program.
